主要内容: The U.S. Department of the Treasury, in collaboration with the Federal Reserve Bank of New York and the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, released findings from an annual survey on U.S. portfolio holdings of foreign securities at the end of 2011. The survey indicated that U.S. holdings of foreign securities totaled approximately $6.8 trillion, with $4.5 trillion in foreign equity, $2.0 trillion in long-term debt, and $0.4 trillion in short-term debt. The previous survey from 2010 also reported around $6.8 trillion, with a slight shift in equity and long-term debt holdings. The stability in holdings between the two years was attributed to valuation losses on foreign equity and expanded reporting coverage in the 2011 survey. The largest U.S. holdings were in the United Kingdom ($989 billion), Canada ($736 billion), the Cayman Islands ($709 billion), and Japan ($509 billion), collectively accounting for 43% of total U.S. portfolio investment. The data is part of an international effort under the IMF to improve the measurement of portfolio asset holdings.
